svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Lambda durable functions orchestrating Lambda MicroVMs. Durable functions can execute for up to one year, using checkpoints to track progress and replay to recover, and during wait operations the function suspends without incurring compute charges. A MicroVM's maximumDurationInSeconds parameter is the maximum total lifespan of the MicroVM including both running and suspended time, with a range of 1 to 28,800 seconds or eight hours, after which Lambda terminates it. Suspending a MicroVM to reduce cost therefore does not extend its lifespan, because suspended time counts against the same ceiling. The maximum idle duration before automatic suspension is also capped at 28,800 seconds, and a separate suspended duration setting terminates a MicroVM after it has been suspended for a configured number of seconds. TERMINATED is a terminal state and the MicroVM cannot be resumed or restarted, so a durable function that outlives its sandbox must treat the MicroVM as an expiring resource rather than a worker. Lambda does not automatically retry durable executions on failure, unlike asynchronous invocations of functions without durable execution, so a dead-letter queue is required to avoid losing the triggering event. Because replay re-runs code from the beginning while skipping completed checkpoints, renaming a step or altering its behaviour while executions are in progress can cause those executions to fail to resume or produce incorrect results, and with executions lasting up to a year the window of in-flight work a deploy can break is correspondingly long. On isolation, each MicroVM runs Amazon Linux 2023, all requests to a MicroVM endpoint require a JWE authentication token and there is no unauthenticated access option, but anything unique the application generates during the image build such as unique IDs, secrets or network connections is shared across all MicroVMs run from the same image version, so per-sandbox values must be generated after start through the run hook, whose payload is unique to each MicroVM and capped at 16 KB. Lambda routes inbound requests by port and does not filter them by URL path, so lifecycle hooks should be hosted on a dedicated port separate from the application port and excluded from the ports a token allows. If the run hook fails or times out the MicroVM may transition directly to terminating without ever reaching running, and if a resume does not succeed Lambda returns 502 Bad Gateway to the caller.
svg.title: The orchestrator gets a year, the MicroVM gets eight hours
svg.text: Two halves of one feature, three orders of magnitude apart.
“The maximum total lifespan of the MicroVM, including both running and suspended time.”
The clocks do not match, and only one of them stops when idle
durable execution up to 1 year waits suspend, no compute charges
MicroVM lifespan 1 - 28,800 s RUNNING and SUSPENDED time both count
Suspension changes the bill, not the deadline. Eight hours of wall clock either way.
TERMINATED IS TERMINAL
“The MicroVM cannot be resumed or restarted.”
Two ways to lose one you were not using:
the 8-hour total, and suspendedDurationSeconds
So the orchestrator rebuilds. It cannot reconnect.
THE RETRY THAT IS NOT THERE
“Unlike asynchronous invocations of functions
without durable execution, Lambda does not
automatically retry durable executions.”
A DLQ holds the only copy of the triggering event.
Replay is the programming model, so a deploy reaches backwards
“During replay, your code runs from the beginning but skips over completed checkpoints.”
Rename a step mid-flight and those executions “can fail to resume or produce incorrect results”
— and in-flight means anything started up to a year ago. Pin to a version or alias.
The sandbox isolates the runtime. The snapshot is shared.
“If your application generates unique content during the build (such as unique IDs, secrets, or network
connections), that content is shared across all MicroVMs run from the same image version.”
Generate per-sandbox values in the /run hook instead. Its payload is per-MicroVM, capped at 16 KB.
For untrusted or agent-generated code, this is the first thing to audit.
Routing is by port, not path — a token covering the hook port can call suspend, resume and terminate. Use a separate port.
Every request needs a JWE token: “There is no unauthenticated access option.” Each MicroVM runs Amazon Linux 2023.
A failed /run hook can go straight to TERMINATING without ever reaching RUNNING. A failed resume returns 502.
Suspended MicroVMs still count against the account memory quota. Only termination frees capacity.
Developer preview, TypeScript and Python — two of the seven languages the durable execution SDK supports.
